articles.title: The Art of Bridal Jewellery
articles.excerpt: A bridal set is never one jewel — it is a composition. Here is how our karigars balance heirloom weight with modern grace.
articles.body:
Every Mangalam bridal commission begins with a conversation — about the wedding, the silks, the moments the bride will treasure. Only then do our designers begin sketching, composing necklaces, jhumkas, bangles and tikka as one harmonious whole.

The craft itself follows generations of Gujarati technique: hand-drawn gold wire, stone-by-stone setting, and a final polish that gives every surface its quiet glow. A single bridal set can pass through more than two hundred hours of skilled hands.

Our advice to every bride: choose one hero piece that feels unmistakably yours, and let the rest of the set support it. Trends will come and go — the jewel you feel beautiful in is the one you will keep forever.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoTitle: The Art of Bridal Jewellery — Mangalam Journal
articles.seoDesc: A bridal set is never one jewel — it is a composition. Here is how our karigars balance heirloom weight with modern grace.

articles.title: Understanding Gold Purity
articles.excerpt: 22K or 18K? Karats, hallmarks and what they truly mean for the jewellery you wear every day.
articles.body:
Gold purity is measured in karats. Pure gold is 24K — too soft for everyday wear — so it is blended with alloys to create 22K, beloved in Gujarati households for its rich warmth, and 18K, favoured for diamond-set designs that need extra strength.

Every Mangalam piece carries a BIS hallmark, your assurance of the exact purity stamped on it. We recommend 22K for traditional pieces and heirloom bangles, and 18K for rings, bracelets and modern silhouettes worn daily.

When in doubt, ask us. Understanding purity is not technical — it is simply the difference between jewellery you admire and jewellery you trust.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoDesc: 22K or 18K? Karats, hallmarks and what they truly mean for the jewellery you wear every day.

articles.title: Gujarati Jewellery Heritage
articles.excerpt: From patlas to pansets — the motifs, rituals and artistry that shape every Mangalam creation.
articles.body:
Gujarat's jewellery tradition is one of India's oldest living crafts. Every region carries its own signature — the layered rani haar of Saurashtra, the geometric kundan of Kutch, the temple-inspired gold of the southern plains.

Our karigars grew up with these forms. The paisley, the peacock, the flowering vine — these are not printed decorations but hand-carved memories, passed from master to apprentice across generations.

At Mangalam, heritage is not preserved behind glass. It is worn to weddings, gifted at births, and reimagined each season — so that tradition continues to live, glitter and evolve.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoDesc: From patlas to pansets — the motifs, rituals and artistry that shape every Mangalam creation.

articles.title: Choosing Your Signature Piece
articles.excerpt: One jewel that feels like you. Here's how to find it — and why it matters more than a full collection.
articles.body:
Most women own many jewels but wear only a few. The pieces we reach for share something: they suit our skin, our routine and our personality without effort. That is a signature piece.

Start with honesty about your life — do you type all day, drape saris on weekends, dress up once a season? A sleek diamond band may serve you better than a grand polki choker, or quite the opposite.

Visit us for a private consultation and we will help you try pieces slowly, in good light, without pressure. The right jewel announces itself the moment you stop thinking about it.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoTitle: Choosing Your Signature Piece — Mangalam Journal
articles.seoDesc: One jewel that feels like you. Here's how to find it — and why it matters more than a full collection.

articles.title: Jewellery Care Guide
articles.excerpt: Simple rituals to keep gold glowing and diamonds brilliant for the decades to come.
articles.body:
Gold asks for little: keep it away from perfume and chlorine, wipe it gently with a soft cloth after wear, and store each piece separately so surfaces never scratch each other.

Diamonds are the hardest natural material but love collecting everyday film. A soak in warm water with a drop of mild soap, a gentle brush, and a pat dry restores their fire in minutes.

Bring your Mangalam pieces home to us once a year. Our karigars will clean, inspect settings and re-polish them — a small service that keeps heirlooms ready for the next generation.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoDesc: Simple rituals to keep gold glowing and diamonds brilliant for the decades to come.

articles.title: Modern Bridal Trends
articles.excerpt: Lighter sets, convertible necklaces and detachable haars — how today's brides are reimagining tradition.
articles.body:
Today's bride wears her jewellery once, then lives in it. That is why convertible design — a choker that becomes a pendant, jhumkas with detachable drops — has become the most requested idea at our atelier.

Weight is moving down and meaning is moving up: brides are choosing fewer, finer pieces with personal motifs — initials in Gujarati script, birthstones beside diamonds, heirloom stones reset into new settings.

Tradition is not being replaced; it is being personalised. A Mangalam bridal set today honours the past and fits the future — exactly as it should.
articles.author: Dhruv Patel
articles.seoDesc: Lighter sets, convertible necklaces and detachable haars — how today's brides are reimagining tradition.

enquiries.name: Ananya Parekh
enquiries.message: Hello, I love the Royal Heritage Necklace. Is it available in a slightly shorter length? I would also like to see it with the matching earrings before my sister's wedding in December.

enquiries.name: Hetal Desai
enquiries.message: We are planning a wedding in February and would like a private bridal consultation for the full set — necklace, jhumkas, bangles and tikka. Are weekend slots available in October?

enquiries.name: Kunal Shah
enquiries.message: Could you share the diamond weight and clarity for this bracelet? I am looking for an anniversary gift and would like it engraved on the clasp if possible.

enquiries.name: Meera Iyer
enquiries.message: I have my grandmother's old kundan pieces. Could your karigars reset the stones into a lighter, modern choker? Happy to bring them in.

reply.text: Thank you, Meera — we would be honoured. Please bring the pieces to Mangalam House; our designer will sketch two options for you on the day.

enquiries.name: Riya Trivedi
enquiries.message: Are the Maharani jhumkas heavy? I would like to wear them through a full day of ceremonies.

reply.text: Hi Riya, each earring weighs about 18 g and has a support chain, so they stay comfortable all day. Would you like to try them in store?

enquiries.name: Aarav Kapadia
enquiries.message: One of the hooks on my kada has loosened. Do you repair pieces bought five years ago?

reply.text: Of course — repairs on Mangalam pieces are free for life. Drop it in any day between 10:30 and 8:30.

enquiries.name: Nisha Mehta
enquiries.message: Do these jhumkas come with screw backs? Buying for my mother.

enquiries.name: Tanvi Rao
enquiries.message: Are you open on Sundays during Navratri? We would like to visit as a family.

enquiries.name: Devang Bhatt
enquiries.message: Can the halo ring be made in 18K rose gold? Ring size 14.

appointments.name: Hetal Desai
appointments.notes: Full bridal set; wedding in February. Bring the Rajwadi and Polki sets.
